meta.name: RSI(2) dip buy
meta.cadence: Checked once a day, after the US close
meta.idea: Buys a sharp, short-lived drop in an index that is in a long-term uptrend, then sells the bounce.
rules: Signal: the 2-day RSI closes below 5 while the ETF closes above its 200-day average.
Entry: buy at that day’s close.
Stop: 2 × ATR(14) below the entry.
Exit: the first close with RSI(2) above 65, or after 5 trading days.
Size: risk 1% of this strategy’s paper equity per trade.

evidence.numbers: Core figures reproduced (win rate, profit factor, drawdown)

meta.name: IBS dip buy
meta.cadence: Checked once a day, after the US close
meta.idea: Buys when a day closes at the very bottom of its own range, then sells once it recovers.
rules: Signal: Internal Bar Strength (close − low) ÷ (high − low) below 0.05.
Entry: buy at that day’s close.
Stop: 2 × ATR(14) below the entry.
Exit: the first close with IBS above 0.75, or after 7 trading days.
Size: risk 1% of this strategy’s paper equity per trade.

evidence.numbers: Reproduced, including the report’s tight variant exactly

meta.name: Funding carry
meta.cadence: Funding is paid every 8 hours; checked daily
meta.idea: Holds the coin and shorts the same amount on the perpetual future, so price moves cancel and the funding payments are the profit.
rules: Signal: the 21-day average of daily funding, annualised, is above 5%.
Entry: open the hedged pair (long spot, short perpetual) at the next day’s start.
Exit: when that annualised average drops below 0%.
Size: 40% of this strategy’s paper equity per coin as spot, with the same amount short.
Costs: 0.2% per side (fees and slippage on both legs).

evidence.numbers: Economics match (funding collected, drawdown); trade count differs

meta.name: Supertrend trend follower
meta.cadence: Checked daily, after the 00:00 UTC candle closes
meta.idea: Follows a new trend on each altcoin, but only in the direction BTC’s long-term trend allows.
rules: Signal: the Supertrend (14, 3) indicator flips direction on the daily close.
Filter: longs only when BTC closes above its 200-day average, shorts only when it is below.
Entry: the next day’s open.
Stop: 3 × ATR(14). Target: 3 × the risk. Time exit: 30 days.
Size: risk 1% of this strategy’s paper equity per trade.

evidence.numbers: 6 of 8 report figures reproduced; return and drawdown were worse

research.headline: The two source reports promised an 85% win rate. None of the strategies came close to that, and the four below are the ones whose edge survived our own re-test.

tested.name: RSI(2) dip buy
tested.note: Beats random entries; 12 of 12 parameter sets profitable.

tested.name: IBS dip buy
tested.note: The report’s tight variant came out identical.

tested.name: Funding carry
tested.note: Real but small, and fading: about +4% in 2025, about +1% in 2026 so far.

tested.name: Supertrend + BTC filter
tested.note: Modest edge; the bootstrap interval still includes zero. Today’s coins only, so survivorship bias is possible.

tested.name: Donchian breakout
tested.note: Not better than random entries; drawdowns of 39% and 81%.

tested.name: Z-score reversion
tested.note: Only 30 trades; loses money when costs double.

cannot: These strategies trade rarely. At the backtested pace the RSI(2) strategy needs about two years to close 30 trades. A few weeks of paper results cannot confirm a win rate.
What the paper account does check: signals fire when they should, fills are realistic, the data feeds hold up, and nothing drifts far from the backtest.
Shorts on altcoins assume a perpetual future is available, and their funding costs are not included.
Carry is shown on the notional it hedges. Real capital also needs margin for the short leg, and a spike can liquidate the short.
